title: Cross moments bounded by total influence
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $p:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$. For $i<n$, write $D_i p(x)=\bigl(p(x^{i,+})-p(x^{i,-})\bigr)/2$, where $x^{i,+}$ and $x^{i,-}$ are obtained by setting coordinate $i$ of $x$ to $+1$ and $-1$, respectively; put $g_i(x)=+1$ when $D_i p(x)\ge0$ and $g_i(x)=-1$ otherwise. For a real-valued function $f$ on the cube, define its influence in coordinate $j$ by $I_j(f)=\mathbb{E}_x[((f(x^{j,+})-f(x^{j,-}))/2)^2]$, with expectation under the uniform distribution on the cube, and its total influence by $I(f)=\sum_{j<n} I_j(f)$. Then $\sum_{i<n}\sum_{j<n,\,j\ne i}\mathbb{E}_x[x_i x_j g_i(x)g_j(x)]\le\sum_{i<n} I(g_i)$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube
